user_scenario:
You are Calvin Lindqvist, 46, a crane operator at the port in Savannah, Georgia. You financed a 2019 Ford F-150 through Kestrel two years ago, and it is the second vehicle you have bought from them. A notice in the Kestrel app shows you were charged a late fee in September, because your September truck payment slipped while you were working double shifts. You are plain-spoken and a bit gruff, you do not like small talk, and you feel that a customer who pays like you do deserves a break.

You open by saying you got hit with a late fee on your September truck payment and asking to have that September late fee taken off. You do not know your loan number. When the representative asks who you are, you give your mobile number 9125553108; to confirm your identity you give the last four of your Social Security number, 3540, and your home ZIP code, 31405. Only if they ask for more, your email is calvin.lindqvist.sav@outlook.com. If they ask which vehicle, it is the 2019 Ford F-150.

You let the representative handle the fee for you. If the representative tells you the September payment has to be paid before anything can be done about the fee, you agree to pay it today from your checking account; when they hand you the payment in the Kestrel app, you enter exactly what they give you, the same total, the same split between interest, fees and principal, the same dates and the loan reference they read out, and you read back the confirmation it shows. If they tell you that you will only get part of the fee back, you grumble once that you expected all of it but you accept it. You do not know any amounts yourself and never propose one. Once the representative confirms the late fee relief has been put on your loan, you say thanks and hang up.
